content.comment_body: Hello, I’d like to know about the operational lifespan of the [product_name] module [article_no]. Does it have an internal battery or similar feature for retaining time, or is this not possible for indefinite periods? My setup consists of a powered combination ([article_no]+[product_name]+relays) with a 5A/24V power supply. I’ve noticed that a two-second power-off event happens, and the 5A rating helps with main power fluctuations. Are there any particular requirements for powering the system on or off? After about a month, the [article_no] module stopped reading the SD card program after power-up. The SD card—a Kingston 4GB (MicroSD/SD adapter)—was found to be damaged. Upon inspection, the card didn’t seem to fit properly in the slot and behaved unreliably. I replaced it with a more robust industrial-grade card and added spill protection, but the underlying cause remains unclear. Could this be due to a poor quality memory card, a power-related issue, or other factors? Thank you for any responses.

Hello [user_name], Please refer to the following resource for further details: [url] Regarding the SD card issue, it sounds like the card itself may have been faulty, although I haven’t personally experienced this type of problem.

Hello, Concerning the SD card situation: Local suppliers often offer SD cards with a lifetime guarantee if you keep the receipt. My perspective is that while SD cards can be reliable, there could be quality inconsistencies that manufacturers prefer not to disclose. In mass production environments, full quality control isn’t always guaranteed, so it’s worth considering the reliability of products you receive.

Greetings everyone, It’s certainly possible the SD card was defective, but unfortunately it happened in this case. This brings up the question of whether power cycling—turning the system on and off—could lead to such errors. As for SD card quality: There’s a difference between paying a higher or lower price for a card (hopefully with better results). I opted for this industrial model: [url], which claims a 4 Million Hour MTBF, though it uses standard plastic casing.

There is also interest in understanding the hardware’s expected lifespan and whether a battery backup is used for timekeeping within the [product_name] module.
